record.paper_title: Open Problems for Entire Functions of Bounded Index in Direction
record.original_question: For an entire function of two variables f(z,w), assume f has bounded L-index in the two coordinate directions (1,0) and (0,1), meaning that in each direction its normalized directional derivatives are controlled by finitely many lower orders using the positive function L. For the ordinary differential equation w'(z) = f(z,w(z)), what one-variable positive function l should be chosen, and under what conditions, so that an entire solution w has bounded l-index in the ordinary one-variable sense?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $f:\mathbb{C}^2\to\mathbb{C}$ be an entire function of two complex variables, and let $L:\mathbb{C}^2\to(0,\infty)$ be a positive continuous function. For a unit direction $\mathbf{b}\in\mathbb{C}^2$, the directional derivative of order $k$ at $(z,w)$ is $\partial^k_{\mathbf{b}} f(z,w)=\frac{d^k}{dt^k}f((z,w)+t\mathbf{b})\big|_{t=0}$. We say that $f$ has bounded $L$-index in the direction $\mathbf{b}$ if there exists $N\in\mathbb{N}$ such that for every $(z,w)\in\mathbb{C}^2$ and every $k\in\mathbb{N}_0$,
$$\frac{|\partial^k_{\mathbf{b}} f(z,w)|}{k!\,L(z,w)^k}\le \max_{0\le j\le N}\frac{|\partial^j_{\mathbf{b}} f(z,w)|}{j!\,L(z,w)^j}.$$
Assume that $f$ has bounded $L$-index in each of the two coordinate directions $\mathbf{b}_1=(1,0)$ and $\mathbf{b}_2=(0,1)$.

For a positive continuous function $l:\mathbb{C}\to(0,\infty)$, an entire function $g:\mathbb{C}\to\mathbb{C}$ has bounded $l$-index (in the ordinary one-variable sense) if there exists $M\in\mathbb{N}$ such that for all $z\in\mathbb{C}$ and all $k\in\mathbb{N}_0$,
$$\frac{|g^{(k)}(z)|}{k!\,l(z)^k}\le \max_{0\le j\le M}\frac{|g^{(j)}(z)|}{j!\,l(z)^j}.$$

Consider the ordinary differential equation
$$w'(z)=f(z,w(z)),\qquad z\in\mathbb{C},$$
and suppose $w$ is an entire solution.

Problem: Determine an explicit choice of the one-variable positive function $l$ (in terms of $L$, $f$, $w$) and sufficient conditions on $f$, $L$, and $w$ under which $w$ necessarily has bounded $l$-index in the ordinary one-variable sense.
artifact.category_tag: Entire functions of bounded L-index in direction
artifact.status_search_result: Search results show active research by Bandura, Skaskiv and others on bounded L-index in direction and applications to entire solutions of directional differential equations and PDEs, including improvements of sufficient conditions. However, no source explicitly resolves this problem in full generality (specifying a canonical choice of one-variable $l$ for general bivariate $f$ with bounded $L$-index in both coordinate directions, for the ODE $w'=f(z,w)$). The problem appears to remain open in full generality, though partial results exist for related PDE/ODE settings.

status_evidence.title: Properties of entire solutions of some linear PDE's
status_evidence.snippet: Improved sufficient conditions of boundedness of L-index in a direction for entire solutions of some linear partial differential equations.
status_evidence.claim: Partial progress exists on related boundedness-of-index questions for entire solutions of directional differential equations.

status_evidence.title: Entire Bivariate Functions of Unbounded Index in Each Direction
status_evidence.snippet: Bivariate entire functions and questions of bounded/unbounded index in coordinate directions.
status_evidence.claim: The setting of bounded index in each coordinate direction is an active research topic, indicating the problem is not trivially settled.

status_evidence.title: Boundedness of L-Index for the Composition of Entire Functions of Several Variables
status_evidence.snippet: Conditions for the composition to inherit bounded index from a one-variable function with bounded l-index.
status_evidence.claim: Related but distinct results on inheritance of bounded index in compositional settings.
